key_insight: A modified quantum annealing eigensolver on D-Wave hardware can estimate magnetic dipole hyperfine structure constants, extending quantum annealing beyond energy calculations to atomic properties.
engineering_relevance: This demonstrates a practical hybrid quantum workflow for small relativistic atomic Hamiltonians, with potential relevance to future quantum-enabled materials and atomic-structure computations.
method: Used a modified QAE with zooming and sigma-annealing.
Encoded eigenvectors with a floating-point scheme and limited precision to three decimal places.
Applied CSF truncation for larger correlation spaces and solved small Dirac-Coulomb Hamiltonian matrices.
evidence_signal: D-Wave QPU results were reported as fully consistent with GRASP at the chosen precision for Li, Be, Na, and Mg HFS constants, with accuracy depending on matrix size.
watch_item: The approach is currently limited to small Hamiltonians and low-precision encoding, so scalability and accuracy on larger correlated systems remain concerns.
paper_title: Applications of quantum annealing to magnetic dipole hyperfine structure constants: First results beyond energies for atoms
